lyrics:
[Intro: soft electric piano, bass, a quiet horn figure]

[Verse 1: warm, low, hesitant]
Couldn't say when the morning turned to you
It was grey, then it wasn't, that's all I knew
One day a coat on the hook that wasn't mine
Next day a second cup, a second line

[Pre-Chorus: climbing step by step, drums building]
Step
By step
Closer
One more step

[Chorus: full band, horns answer, crowd shouts the replies]
Hey, Rosalie (da, da, da)
Monday never looked so fine
(That's right, that's right)
I've got a mind (da, da, da)
To tell the whole street you're mine
(Go on, then)

[Verse 2: warm, a little bolder]
Now the hallway's got two umbrellas in the stand
And I'm learning how to walk while holding a hand
I was quiet, I was careful, I was fine
Then you laughed in my kitchen, and it's been a long time

[Pre-Chorus: climbing step by step, drums building]
Step
By step
Closer
One more step

[Chorus: full band, horns answer, crowd shouts the replies]
Hey, Rosalie (da, da, da)
Monday never looked so fine
(That's right, that's right)
I've got a mind (da, da, da)
To tell the whole street you're mine
(Go on, then)

[Instrumental: horns play the chorus melody, crowd clapping]

[Final Chorus: everyone, key up a step, crowd at full voice]
Hey, Rosalie (da, da, da)
Monday never looked so fine
(That's right, that's right)
I've got a mind (da, da, da)
To tell the whole street you're mine
(Go on, then)
Hey, Rosalie

[Outro: horns, crowd cheering, fade]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 126 BPM, 4/4, B major, lifting a step for the last chorus. A quiet, careful verse and a big, open, swaying chorus built for a crowd.

VOICE: Male baritone, warm, grainy and close in the verses, almost talking. He opens up to a broad, full-voiced, friendly shout in the chorus. A crowd sings the horn notes ('da, da, da') and shouts the bracketed replies.

INSTRUMENTS: Electric piano and a soft bass in the verses. A horn section (trumpets and trombones) that plays a quiet rising figure and then three bright notes after the title in each chorus. A drum kit that builds through the pre-chorus. A string section. Acoustic guitar strum. Tambourine and handclaps.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, electric piano and a quiet horn figure. 0:12 Verse 1. 0:36 Pre-chorus, four steps upward. 0:46 Chorus 1 with crowd replies. 1:08 Verse 2. 1:32 Pre-chorus. 1:42 Chorus 2. 2:04 Instrumental, horns on the tune with clapping. 2:18 The key lifts for the final chorus. 2:44 Outro, horns and cheering, fading by 2:58.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Late-1960s pop: warm and intimate in the verse, wide and brassy in the chorus, with the crowd mixed in as part of the band.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The first three horn notes and the crowd's reply at 0:48.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The love arrives as household evidence: a coat, a cup, two umbrellas. He was 'quiet, careful and fine' before. It reads as a second chance later in life, and the day celebrated is a Monday.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Hesitation, growing nerve, public joy.
